backend/servers/api-server/src/services/jwt.rs:198-212 (validate_access_token) and :216-230 (validate_refresh_token) build `Validation::default()` and set only `validation.validate_exp = true`. Neither validator binds `aud` (audience) or `iss` (issuer): there is no `validation.set_audience(...)` / `validation.set_issuer(...)` call, and the issued Claims struct (:30-57) carries no aud/iss fields at all. Token scoping rests solely on the shared HS256 secret plus the string `token_type` gate (:208 `!= "access"`, :226 `!= "refresh"`).

Consequence: any component that shares JWT_SECRET (api-server is also the OAuth provider per CLAUDE.md, and reality-server is an SSO consumer against the same shared DB/auth surface) will accept a token minted for a different audience/context. There is no cryptographic binding preventing an access token issued for one principal-kind/service context from being replayed against another that trusts the same secret. The nbf (not-before) claim is likewise unvalidated.

A job is popped off the list via BLPOP (process_pending_jobs :1601, queue_pop_blocking on PUSH_FANOUT_QUEUE_KEY :1486, up to MAX_JOBS_PER_TICK=256 :1498 per tick). On a GENUINE transient failure the job is logged and DROPPED with no re-queue, no backoff, and no dead-letter: the `Err(e) =>` arm at the end of deliver_job (~:1683-1697) carries the inline comment "Genuine failure (DB error or all provider sends failed). ... we log and move on rather than re-queue (avoids hot-looping on a permanently failing job)" and only emits `tracing::warn!(... "push delivery failed for queued job")`. Because the payload was already BLPOP-popped off the list before delivery is attempted, a TRANSIENT fault — an FCM/APNs 5xx or rate-limit, a momentary Postgres pool exhaustion while resolving device tokens, or a Redis/network blip mid-send — permanently loses that user's push notification for the remaining process lifetime. The queue's at-least-once intent (BLPOP drain of a durable Redis list) is silently downgraded to at-most-once for every transient blip. The code conflates PERMANENT failures (which correctly should not re-queue, to avoid the poison-message hot-loop the comment guards against) with TRANSIENT ones (which SHOULD get bounded retry/backoff or a dead-letter list). NET-NEW vs backlog: distinct FILE+MECHANISM from code-review-api-core-quiet-drain-drops-failed-delivery (that is quiet_hours_drain.rs's DB-held deliver_held drain, not the Redis BLPOP queue worker) and distinct from all prior push_fanout token/endpoint findings. Reachability traced statically (process_pending_jobs -> deliver_job -> adapter.send); runtime frequency of transient-vs-permanent not confirmed, hence confidence medium.
